notice: The docstring is the tool description the model reads, including the negative instruction "Do NOT use to place orders". Descriptions drive tool selection, so they are prompt engineering.
Unknown SKUs raise `ToolError`, which reaches the model as an `is_error` result with your message. Any other exception is treated as a crash and the model sees only a generic message.
Resources are addressed by URI (`catalog://all`) and are read-only; prompts take arguments and return messages. Same server, three primitives, three different controllers.

notice: A stdio server waits on stdin, so "still running" is the healthy result. It does not listen on a port, which is the security property that makes stdio the default for local servers.
stdout is reserved for protocol messages; logs belong on stderr. A stray print() in a stdio server corrupts the stream, a classic cause of a server that connects and then fails.

checkpoint.q: Name the three primitives and who controls each
checkpoint.a: Tools are model-controlled: the model decides when to invoke them. Resources are application-controlled: the client decides what data to attach as context. Prompts are user-controlled: templates the user picks, often surfaced as slash commands. An exam stem about who triggers the capability is asking you to map it to one of these.

checkpoint.q: Which transport for a local process? Which for remote?
checkpoint.a: stdio for a local process: the client launches the server as a subprocess and talks over stdin and stdout, with no network exposure. Streamable HTTP for a remote server reached by URL, which should be authenticated. The older HTTP+SSE transport is deprecated, so it is the wrong answer for a new remote server.

checkpoint.q: When is an MCP server the right answer instead of a custom tool?
checkpoint.a: When the capability must be reusable across applications or hosts (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, other MCP clients) or maintained by a different team. A custom tool defined in one app's API call serves only that app. The buried constraint to look for is "reusable" or "shared across".
